mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 3.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of FEDFUNDS-triggered periods above 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST monthly decline > 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes with both GDPC1 and HOUST conditions met.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate hiring, which in turn depresses earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly lower (p > 0.10) in triggered periods compared to non-triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of INDPRO-triggered contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% combined with a concurrent decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 1.5% for two months signals a deflationary easing environment, which historically has been associated with positive equity risk premia and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL < 1.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly higher (p < 0.05) in triggered deflationary easing episodes compared to baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth above 250k per month for three consecutive months signals a robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 250000 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly higher (p < 0.10) in triggered periods compared to non-triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) of more than 1% signals a broad-based demand shock, which is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to rapid repricing of risk.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -1% AND HOUST monthly change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes with both GDPC1 and HOUST conditions met.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between industrial production (INDPRO) growth and S&P 500 forward returns exists in expansionary regimes; when INDPRO monthly growth exceeds 0.5%, the S&P 500 tends to deliver positive 20-day returns.
failure_condition: The conditional probability of positive S&P 500 20-day returns given INDPRO > 0.5% monthly growth is not significantly above 60% (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample tests.
